queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: What passes cannot fill the heart; turning toward what lasts gives each day a quiet purpose.
queries.act: Turn toward what lasts: serve, study, reflect daily, and offer your work to something beyond yourself.

hook.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
hook.setting: Letter from Alameda, California, 18 April 1900, after laying down his role as leader.
hook.line: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
hook.translation: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
hook.why: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

prasang.title: 'I am drifting': a letter from Alameda (1900)
prasang.summary: Two years before his death, worn out, he writes that he has laid down the role of leader. He is glad he was born, glad he suffered, glad he made big blunders. He admits that ambition, personality, fear and love of power lay behind his work, and says they are fading as he drifts toward peace.
prasang.lesson: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
alternates.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
alternates.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
alternates.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
alternates.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Worship of Shiva
prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.setting: From the section praising learning: the blessings of a good life.
alternates.sanskrit: सूनुः सच्चरितः सती प्रियतमा स्वामी प्रसादोन्मुखः स्निग्धं मित्रमवञ्चकः परिजनो निष्क्लेशलेशं मनः । आकारो रुचिरः स्थिरश्च विभवो विद्यावदातं मुखं तुष्टे विष्टपकष्टहारिणि हरौ सम्प्राप्यते देहिना ॥
alternates.line: A good child, a loving spouse, a kind boss, a true friend, a mind at ease: count these as grace.
alternates.translation: A son of good conduct, a devoted and loving wife, a gracious master, an affectionate friend, kinsfolk who do not cheat, a mind without a trace of strain, a pleasing form, lasting prosperity, a face bright with learning: these come to the one with whom Hari, remover of the world's troubles, is pleased.
alternates.why: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
prasang.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
verse.translation: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: Even in success and failure doesn't mean indifferent to them; learn from both without being thrown.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.try_today: Notice the gratitude without holding on to it.
verse.scene_line: You watch the new life beside the steady hand that offered thanks.

why: Your part is the work (Bhagavad Gita 2.47-50)

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on worship for rewards and worship without desire.
verse.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
verse.line: Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.
verse.translation: To those who think of me alone and worship me, ever devoted, I bring what they lack and preserve what they have.
verse.why: Trust eases the worry of getting and keeping.
verse.misuse: Not 'God will pay the bills, so don't plan'. Trust eases worry; it doesn't replace effort or prudence.

prasang.title: Worship with and without desire, and their fruits
prasang.summary: Those who worship for heavenly rewards return when merit runs out; those who think of him alone are carried and protected.
prasang.lesson: Trust eases the worry of getting and keeping.

verse.for_you: You have a new granddaughter and both are healthy. You want to hold on to this gratitude. Let the feeling itself be the thanks you give.
verse.try_today: Let this gratitude be the whole offering today.
verse.scene_line: You hold your granddaughter while Krishna carries what you lack and guards what you have.

why: Rama's vow of safety to whoever comes afraid; 'I carry what they lack'.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः । लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
verse.line: Janaka and others reached fulfilment through action. Keep working, if only for the good of the world.
verse.translation: Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. And looking to the welfare of the world, you too should act.
verse.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.for_you: Your granddaughter is here, and your heart is full. That gratitude is a living action. Let it guide the good you still want to offer the world.
verse.try_today: Notice one small act today that benefits someone else.
verse.scene_line: You stand beside Krishna and Janaka, whose work was always for the good of the world.

why: acting for the holding together of the world

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: The most quoted lines of the graduation address.
verse.sanskrit: देवपितृकार्याभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । मातृदेवो भव । पितृदेवो भव । आचार्यदेवो भव । अतिथिदेवो भव ।
verse.line: Treat your mother as divine, your father as divine, your teacher as divine, your guest as divine.
verse.translation: Do not neglect your duties to the gods and the ancestors. Let your mother be a god to you. Let your father be a god to you. Let your teacher be a god to you. Let your guest be a god to you.
verse.why: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.
verse.misuse: Honouring parents does not mean accepting mistreatment or giving up your own conscience.

prasang.title: The graduation address
prasang.summary: As a student finishes his studies and leaves to start family life, the teacher gives him parting instructions: speak truth, do right, keep learning, honour mother, father, teacher and guest, give with grace. He even tells the student to copy only the teachers' good conduct, and when in doubt to act as thoughtful, gentle people would.
prasang.lesson: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

verse.for_you: You hold a new life in your hands. Let your gratitude be the offering you give to those who came before you.
verse.try_today: Offer a quiet thank you to the ones who raised you today.
verse.scene_line: You see your granddaughter and know the line of life continues through you.

why: the guest and the elder are served as sacred
those who raised and taught you are to be honoured as one honours a deity

verse.speaker: Sampati
verse.setting: The monkeys despair at the ocean; the old vulture Sampati rouses them.
verse.sanskrit: पापिउ जाकर नाम सुमिरहीं। अति अपार भवसागर तरहीं॥ तासु दूत तुम्ह तजि कदराई राम हृदयँ धरि करहु उपाई ॥
verse.line: Drop your timidity. Keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
verse.translation: Even sinners who remember his name cross the boundless ocean of the world. You are his messengers: give up your timidity, keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
verse.for_you: You have a grandchild, and you want to hold on to this feeling. Keep this joy in your heart and let it guide your day.
verse.try_today: Hold the feeling of gratitude in your heart as you move through the day.
verse.scene_line: You stand here, holding a new life, while the messengers of Ram prepare to leap.

why: act with Ram held in the heart

story.title: A king and queen serve a guest who seems determined to break them
story.story_hook: The guest burned the feast, then had the king and queen pull his chariot. They did not get angry once.
story.summary: The sage Chyavana comes to King Kushika's palace and asks to be served. He sleeps for days and the king and queen must sit by him without rest. He orders a huge feast, then has it burned along with the bed and seat (13.88.21-22). He has them yoked to a chariot and drives them through the streets, striking them. Through all of it they show no anger (13.88.23).
story.lesson: Service without resentment, under provocation, is the strongest proof of a good heart.
story.teaser: The guest burned the feast, then had the king and queen pull his chariot. They did not get angry once.
story.for_you: Your granddaughter and her mother are healthy, and you want to hold on to this gratitude. A good heart needs no provocation to be good. Let this quiet joy stay with you today.
